name: Non-central nervous system-localized embryonal carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and clinical diagnostic criteria for embryonal carcinoma

criteria.description: Identification of embryonal carcinoma cells on biopsy with characteristic primitive epithelial morphology
Radiologic evidence of a localized mass outside the central nervous system consistent with embryonal carcinoma
Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels supporting diagnosis
Exclusion of central nervous system involvement by clinical and imaging studies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of embryonal carcinoma cells in a non-CNS localized tumor with supportive imaging and exclusion of CNS involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on tissue biopsy and immunohistochemical staining; tumor markers aid but are not definitive alone.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable non-CNS localized mass with rapid growth
pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a firm, enlarging mass in gonadal or extragonadal sites
searchTerms: fast-growing lump outside brain or spinal cord

pathognomonic.notes: Reflects tumor secretion, useful for diagnosis and monitoring

common.symptomName: Localized pain or discomfort at tumor site
common.notes: Due to mass effect or local invasion

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms including weight loss and night sweats
searchTerms: weight loss with fever and night sweating
general symptoms like fatigue and sweating at night
unexplained weight loss and night sweats

common.notes: May be elevated in some cases, aiding diagnosis

common.symptomName: Swelling or enlargement of involved extragonadal sites
common.notes: Common in mediastinal or retroperitoneal tumors

occasional.symptomName: Dyspnea due to mediastinal mass effect
occasional.notes: Occurs if tumor compresses airways or lungs
searchTerms: shortness of breath from chest mass
breathing difficulty due to mediastinal tumor

occasional.notes: From retroperitoneal or abdominal tumor involvement
Due to hormonal secretion by tumor

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to paraneoplastic syndromes
rare.notes: Rarely observed in non-CNS embryonal carcinoma
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from cancer-related immune effects
neurological signs due to paraneoplastic syndrome
nerve problems linked to cancer immune response

rare.notes: If pulmonary metastases or invasion present

imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing localized extragonadal mass
Chest X-ray or CT for mediastinal masses
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may be present in tumor tissue
other: Histopathology demonstrating primitive epithelial tumor cells with immunohistochemical positivity for CD30 and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mixed germ cell tumor elements
Histopathology showing multiple germ cell components
Presence of differentiated tissues from multiple germ layers
Lack of primitive embryonal carcinoma cells on biopsy
Absence of elevated AFP or β-hCG

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with local invasion
Elevated tumor markers AFP and β-hCG
Respiratory distress or superior vena cava syndrome from mediastinal involvement
